decision: Use the event log as the only source of truth; every application view is a replayable projection.
rationale: This is the plan's deliberate irreversible bet and enables provenance, compensation, replay, and adapter replacement.

decision: Use content-derived, user-editable handles with historical aliases and positional collision fallbacks.
rationale: Natural-language referenceability is a core product affordance.

decision: Keep a closed block taxonomy in v1 while retaining a string type and JSON property seam.
rationale: Specific types preserve intent; the property map keeps later additions additive.

decision: Use one per-user event stream and derive aggregate boundaries as projections.
rationale: It keeps append ordering and replay semantics simple for the first implementation.

decision: Use a discriminated event union behind one append boundary with actor-by-type permissions.
rationale: It preserves a stable model tool contract while enforcing the addendum's producer rules server-side.

decision: Include client_id and compensates_event_id in the first persisted envelope.
rationale: Both are unbackfillable and required for concurrency and semantically correct undo.

decision: Keep erasable natural-language content outside the immutable log and store pointers in payloads.
rationale: This supports a future legal and erasure posture without weakening the audit log.

decision: Collections are authored trees with one parent per item, sibling-scoped handles, fractional positions, and an implicit root.
rationale: Tree to multi-membership is additive; the reverse requires cleanup. Filing must remain a user act.

decision: Pin the production target to Postgres 17 plus pgvector and TimescaleDB, while using D1 for this deployable product slice.
rationale: The attached plan owns the production stack decision; the Sites runtime provides a portable SQLite demonstration of the same append contract.
reversal_cost: low for this slice; medium for production

decision: Select at least two image-model providers.
rationale: Commercial and product choice; adapter placeholders remain provider-neutral.

decision: Set capture scope and privacy posture.
rationale: The surveillance-perception line is a values choice; ambient capture remains disabled.

decision: Set scout, prompt, and monthly cost ceilings.
rationale: Spend authority cannot be delegated; all paid autonomous work remains disabled.

decision: Choose retention, derived-memory rights, and legal posture before Phase 6 telemetry.
rationale: Compliance and data rights require accountable human ownership.

decision: Choose personal, team, or community library and sharing scope before Phase 10.
rationale: The choice changes moderation, identity, and infrastructure requirements.

decision: Replace the React and vinext UI runtime with Lit custom elements on a plain Vite and Cloudflare Worker application shell.
rationale: The authoritative plan selects standards-first custom elements; direct routing preserves D1 and R2 while removing framework-specific UI state.

decision: Isolate signal-polyfill and signal-utils behind the FormaStore boundary.
rationale: The user requested the TC39 Signals proposal stack, while both upstream packages describe themselves as experimental; isolation keeps component contracts stable if the proposal changes.

decision: Keep administrative long-stream scenarios theoretical and in-memory until explicitly exported; never append them to the durable user stream.
rationale: The replay lab needs scale and explanation fixtures without contaminating product truth or incurring durable storage costs.

decision: Expose every human-blocked phase through a functional simulation or governance surface while keeping external execution disabled.
rationale: This completes the ecosystem outline without assuming provider, privacy, budget, legal, or sharing decisions the kickoff addendum reserves for accountable humans.

decision: Use the OpenAI Responses API with gpt-5.6-terra as the first live provider adapter.
rationale: A server-side structured-output adapter activates one production provider while keeping the compiler contract replaceable.

decision: Allow explicit product interactions only; prohibit passive device, microphone, dwell-time, and ambient capture.
rationale: The pilot should earn trust through visible authored actions and event receipts.

decision: Enforce monthly hard caps of 250,000 tokens per user and 2,500,000 tokens per workspace with preflight reservations.
rationale: Race-safe reservation prevents paid work after either ceiling is reached; limits remain configurable without code changes.

decision: Treat submitted work as user-controlled, require explicit rights assertions for external assets, and redact private prompt/provider content after 30 days.
rationale: Immutable events keep non-sensitive receipts while erasable content supports the adopted privacy posture.

decision: Use private-by-default read-only links that expire within seven days and can be revoked immediately.
rationale: This enables bounded pilot collaboration without granting append authority or adopting community publishing.

decision: Accept one live provider adapter for the Phase 2 pilot instead of the planned two-provider acceptance bar.
rationale: The user explicitly accepted the debt so the deterministic quality and re-entry milestones can proceed without treating provider diversity as complete.
reversal_cost: low while the prompt-plane contract remains provider-neutral
revisit_trigger: Before Phase 7 production rollout or general availability, add a second adapter and run the same-context comparison.

decision: Gate Phase 3 deterministic extractors at no more than a 10% correction rate globally and per extractor on the frozen v1 corpus.
rationale: With three checks per extractor, one incorrect result blocks the gate; confidence remains visible but cannot substitute for correctness.
reversal_cost: low; revise only with a versioned corpus and recorded rationale

decision: Require at least ten witnessed brief-item impressions before the Phase 6 pilot is ready for a human go/no-go review.
rationale: Ten impressions are a sufficiency floor for reviewing acceptance, cost, and dosage together, not an automatic success threshold or a substitute for judgment.
reversal_cost: low; tune from recorded pilot evidence

decision: Use a deterministic, versioned local embedding projection for the private Phase 7 pilot while preserving the production pgvector/HNSW contract.
rationale: The pilot can validate family correction, collection-filter metadata, cited retrieval, and rebuild semantics without new credentials or treating disposable vectors as truth. Production scale and a representative licensed corpus remain explicit gates.
reversal_cost: low; replacing the embedding model is a full projection rebuild
revisit_trigger: Before Phase 7 production rollout, alongside D-0019 provider diversity debt and the pgvector/HNSW migration.

decision: Make every re-entry brief item carry an exact replayable destination, and define blank canvas as creation of a new current document rather than reuse of the previous projection.
rationale: A continuity suggestion is trustworthy only when it opens the cited comparison, block, or collection. Starting blank must provide a real opt-out while the append-only stream and Library retain earlier work.

decision: Collect the initial document name before creating a blank canvas, create no context blocks as a side effect, and append a direction only after the user authors and submits it.
rationale: An empty named document is a meaningful event-sourced state. Pre-populating a placeholder converts an opt-out into an inferred creative choice and makes the provenance misleading; later names and content remain explicit correction events.

decision: Treat upload rights, block type, block order, removal, and reference-derived palette adoption as explicit authored interactions with reversible event receipts; keep source-reference palettes read-only.
rationale: A native confirmation dialog cannot explain the consequence or preserve context, generic Direction blocks erase user intent, and editing extracted evidence in place confuses inference with authorship. Dedicated dialogs and typed events preserve both usability and provenance.

decision: Advance Phase 6 with continued evidence collection; activate bounded report-only Scout runs and a ranking-only, reversible taste pilot with a visible 60-day exponential half-life.
rationale: The witnessed impression floor, acceptance view, cost view, and dosage cohorts are sufficient for a human advance decision without pretending the sample is complete. Continuing measurement preserves learning while Phases 8 and 9 exercise their authority and budget boundaries.
reversal_cost: low; gate status, scout envelopes, and decay parameters remain versioned
revisit_trigger: Review Slice 6 acceptance and dosage as the sample grows; tune the Phase 9 decay only from witnessed promotion and critique evidence.

decision: Render image and palette viewers in the dialog top layer, allow light-dismiss with closedby=any plus a target-equality fallback, and permit palette samples only from pixels in the cited reference image.
rationale: A dialog positioned inside a context block can switch containment as surrounding layout changes, while unrestricted color inputs make sampled evidence indistinguishable from arbitrary authored colors. Top-layer dialogs and explicit next-swatch feedback keep both interaction and provenance stable.

decision: Project all documents as navigable event-sourced state, distinguish recent outputs from explicitly kept outputs, and require every Library or Studio affordance to expose its destination or disabled condition.
rationale: A successful append that leaves the user on the same page appears inert; an invisible library flag has no product meaning; and generic navigation conceals the relationship among documents, context, outputs, and collections. Focused previews and DocumentOpened receipts make the content graph usable without weakening provenance.

decision: Permit explicit opt-in collection of coarse attention episodes only while the Forma page is visible; exclude raw pointer paths, coordinates, keys, typed text, microphone, and ambient device data; cap downstream authority at 0.25 of a direct action.
rationale: Semantic dwell windows linked to visible object IDs and their ending actions can reveal product friction and strengthen already-explicit intent without treating presence as authorship. Idle time, page exits, and machine-away periods are discounted; device detail expires after 14 days, durable summaries carry an expiry and are ignored after a user forgets them.
revisit_trigger: Review false-positive friction flags, opt-in rate, and confirmed Scout judgments before widening contexts, retention, or signal authority.

decision: Add a Creative Editor lens that represents the complete durable document through a familiar tool palette, artboard, preview, and contextual inspector while omitting event-log and provenance machinery from the working surface.
rationale: A user should be able to shape a complete creative document without learning event types, handles, authority labels, sequence counts, or projection terminology. Plain-language actions remain translations onto the same event vocabulary, so reducing conceptual load does not create a second data model or weaken replayability.

decision: Give every document lens a device-local Focus view that removes global, project, introductory, and summary chrome while preserving the document-view switcher and an explicit exit.
rationale: Document lenses need enough width and height to make their interaction model useful. A reversible presentation preference can reclaim the viewport without changing document state, URLs, or event semantics, and keeping the lens switcher visible preserves orientation and escape.

decision: Represent Focus view as a trailing /focus segment on every canonical document-view URL while retaining device preference only as a fallback that canonicalizes into the URL.
rationale: Focused presentation affects how a document can be reviewed and therefore needs the same refresh, sharing, browser-history, document-switching, and lens-switching guarantees as document identity. A path segment keeps presentation state explicit without introducing a second document model.

decision: Represent the affected area of every block with one versioned, document-normalized spatial_scope property shared by all document views.
rationale: Whole-document, fuzzy-region, AABB, subject-relative, and clipping-path targeting need one replayable meaning across responsive editors and generated output sizes. View-local mask state would split the document model and make compiler attribution ambiguous.
reversal_cost: medium; schema versions allow additive target methods without rewriting prior events

decision: Compile Exclusion blocks as explicitly signed must_not_include facts and interpret their weight as exclusion strictness.
rationale: A negative constraint presented with positive prominence language can be mistaken for the subject of the work by both users and model adapters. Signed compiler effects preserve intent without relying on wording or handle conventions.

decision: Make the document preview the primary spatial-scope authoring surface through rectangle drawing and movement, freeform drawing, and fuzzy natural-language entry.
rationale: Normalized coordinates are useful storage and precision controls but are an unnecessarily mechanical primary interaction for visually selecting an affected area.

decision: Make quick-add role selection explicit in rendered form state and allow an existing plan item to be reclassified through a replayable type edit.
rationale: A dialog whose explanatory copy says Avoid while its selector visibly says Goal is not trustworthy. A repair path is also required because durable content created under a former UI defect must be correctable without deletion or silent migration.

decision: Model Include, Prefer, Avoid, and Prohibit as intent applied independently to a block's semantic role and spatial scope.
rationale: Avoid is an operation on a Subject, Mood, Composition, Palette, Material, or other decision—not a semantic role of its own. Keeping role, intent, and scope orthogonal preserves meaning for users, replay, compilation, and model adapters while retaining legacy Exclusion blocks as general negative constraints.

decision: Generate real image artifacts through the direct OpenAI Image API with gpt-image-2 after a bounded structured planning pass, store image bytes in private R2, and keep only authenticated media and model receipts in the event stream.
rationale: The document needs to resolve into an actual reviewable creative artifact rather than decorative CSS. Separating planning from rendering preserves structured explanations and negative constraints, while object storage keeps replay lightweight and lets every document, comparison, library, export, and share surface resolve the same immutable output.
reversal_cost: medium; the event and asset contracts remain provider-neutral

decision: Witness canonical document-view visits as durable structured workflow evidence, analyze direct actions and retained outcomes per view, and keep optional dwell capped as supplemental evidence.
rationale: Re-entry needs a defensible route back into productive work, Scout needs to locate view-specific progress or friction, and Taste & time needs to distinguish working-mode preference from aesthetic preference. Document-view evidence may adapt UI routing and support, but it is excluded from generation context and cannot create taste beliefs.
reversal_cost: low; the event remains additive and the workflow projection is fully rebuildable

decision: Make the visual theme preference-reactive with CSS-native color-scheme and light-dark semantic tokens, without an application theme picker or persisted theme state.
rationale: The browser and operating system remain the source of truth for user display preference, native controls participate automatically, and every route receives one accessible token contract without adding UI or state machinery.

decision: Add Canvas as an independently loaded sibling application with many named canvases per project over the shared block, document, output, collection, user, and membership contracts.
rationale: Spatial collaboration needs distinct route, bundle, and interaction ownership without creating a second creative data model or organizational tree.

decision: Move shared creative truth toward one totally ordered stream per project while retaining per-user streams for sessions, private inference, dismissals, and telemetry residue.
rationale: Team members must converge on one authored history while private memory and consent remain partitioned by person.
revisit_trigger: Dedicated sequencer escalation if per-project append contention breaches the recorded gauge.

decision: Use spec-owned RGA text operations translated through Yjs, per-property max-HLC registers, and observed-remove stroke sets; never extend the shared event envelope for Canvas causality.
rationale: The operation grammar remains replayable and engine-swappable while common concurrent edits converge without serializing raw library encodings.
revisit_trigger: Interleaving-anomaly evidence from the convergence harness.

decision: Keep live names, selections, and cursor positions broadcast-only and always visible on shared canvases; store no cursor or pointer trails, and keep telemetry consent independent from collaboration awareness.
rationale: Awareness prevents ghost edits, while storage of fine-grained movement creates unnecessary surveillance and cannot be justified as creative truth.
revisit_trigger: Material evidence that always-visible presence causes collaboration avoidance.

decision: Treat arrangement as pre-formal organization: proximity, overlap, containment, and z-order do not influence generation until a user emits ContextSetFormalized for a named selection.
rationale: Spatial thinking is useful before it is semantically resolved; hidden compilation from position would make outputs surprising and provenance ambiguous.

decision: Keep arranger and other agent artifacts in project report space until an editor accepts a cited proposal; rejection is restorable and agents cannot self-promote or choose direction.
rationale: Machine work can prepare decisions without becoming authored state or silently moving user work.

decision: Represent every Canvas view and lens in a refresh-safe URL while witnessing no filter, sort, seeded-random, or other derivable lens state.
rationale: People can share and revisit useful views without polluting creative truth with presentation choices.
revisit_trigger: Evidence that heavily circulated lens URLs need authored naming or persistence.

decision: Allow offline authoring through a capped IndexedDB queue, but keep all budget-reserving generation and agent work online-only.
rationale: Creative edits must survive disconnection, while external spend requires current authorization, capacity, and provider state.
revisit_trigger: Legitimate offline work routinely exceeds 14 days, 10000 operations, or 50 MB.

decision: Use project-level viewer, commenter, editor, and owner membership for canvases; editors act symmetrically on unlocked objects, locks are advisory, and administrative overrides are witnessed.
rationale: The same access container should govern documents and blocks without turning temporary manipulation into ownership.

decision: Keep every Canvas capability reachable without inference; later JIT delivery may rank a stable set but may never hide or remove a capability.
rationale: Adaptive salience should reduce hunting without making the product’s powers unpredictable or preference-dependent.

decision: Require GPT Image 2 and Ideogram 4 same-context capability evaluation before Canvas image features reach pilot users; declare sketch conditioning approximated and retain Flux 2 as the named group-3 contingency.
rationale: Text planning does not provide image-adapter diversity, and editing or sketch claims require direct paired evidence.
revisit_trigger: Frozen-corpus capability scores or provider-contract changes.

decision: Permit organization-level shaping only from dual-key consented, ACL-scoped, daily recomputed aggregates with k=5 and silence below the threshold; inferred data may rank but never filter.
rationale: Group-level learning must not expose individual behavior or cross project-access boundaries.
revisit_trigger: Counsel’s finding may require counts-plus-k-met or a higher threshold; nothing lowers k below 5.

decision: Keep Canvas restricted to build-team administrators until a named Trust and Safety owner signs, counsel clears the consent pack, and the second image-adapter contract is in place before image pilot exposure.
rationale: The specification makes accountability, meaningful consent, offline custody, rights propagation, and adapter diversity explicit conditions rather than implementation details.
revisit_trigger: Named owner, recorded legal finding, and adapter procurement receipts are all present.

decision: Undo may compensate only the current member’s own events; changes to another member’s work are new attributed forward acts.
rationale: Collaboration history must not allow one person to erase another person’s authorship through a local undo stack.

decision: Use one project sequencer and shared admission contract: Durable Objects for the pilot topology and Postgres head-row transactions plus non-persisting WebSocket fan-out for production.
rationale: Both environments need the same authorization and merge outcomes while using the operationally appropriate ordering mechanism.
revisit_trigger: Concurrent-append pressure requires a dedicated sequencer service.

decision: Keep every actual-data mock in a replay-owned fictional creator account and let an administrator enter it only through a bounded, visibly persistent impersonation session; never copy a mock project into the administrator’s regular account.
rationale: A separate user, event stream, media namespace, project graph, and behavioral-signal boundary make synthetic experience realistic without contaminating personal projects, memory, taste, Scout, re-entry, or attention evidence. Every modifying interaction requires an explicit per-action confirmation, and cancel, Escape, close, or backdrop dismissal discards the attempted change.
reversal_cost: medium; persona fixtures and impersonation receipts remain append-only
revisit_trigger: A future multi-tenant test-account service provides a stronger isolated identity boundary with the same per-action consent contract.

decision: Persist every user-applied Canvas arrangement as an immutable selection-scoped snapshot containing member IDs, layout policy, and complete before-and-after card frames; keep the resulting per-property geometry registers as the convergent rendering authority.
rationale: A first-class arrangement makes Match size and other organization actions findable, replayable, re-applicable, and atomically undoable without allowing visual proximity or prominence to become hidden generation context.
reversal_cost: low; snapshots can remain historical even if later arrangement editors add mutable names or membership revisions

decision: Enforce monthly hard caps of 500,000 tokens per user and 5,000,000 tokens per workspace with preflight reservations.
rationale: The expanded media and document-rendering workflows need twice the pilot capacity while retaining race-safe reservation, settlement, release, and fail-closed behavior.

decision: Record the product owner's Trust & Safety ownership and counsel-clearance attestations for Canvas, replace the client admin-role gate with a durable server-owned three-requirement policy, and retain the independent second image-adapter contract and passing paired evaluation as the remaining pilot blocker.
rationale: Availability should follow witnessed governance evidence instead of a client feature flag, while an administrator still needs internal access to finish and evaluate the remaining provider work.
revisit_trigger: The provider-independent adapter contract, capability receipt, and frozen-corpus comparison are recorded or any existing approval is revoked.

decision: Use a server-only Fal Ideogram V4 adapter family as the provider-independent image path: Ideogram V4 for full text-to-image, V4 Fast for drafts, and V4 image-to-image for one-reference edits; retain the OpenAI adapter for multi-reference edits and record the capability-based fallback reason.
rationale: The adapter can share the same bounded prompt, safety, rights, failure, durable media, and cost-receipt contracts without claiming features the provider does not expose. Provider selection remains explicit and auditable.
revisit_trigger: A Fal model adds evaluated multi-reference editing, the paired 50-context evaluation fails, or another independent provider offers a materially stronger contract.

decision: Keep Ideogram V4 prompt expansion enabled in the Fal adapter: Medium for draft and balanced work, Large for full quality; retain both application preflight and provider output safety checks.
rationale: The frozen same-context smoke evaluation reproduced post-render safety false positives with expansion disabled. Ideogram's official prompting guide states that V4 is trained on structured JSON captions and unexpanded plain text is likely to trigger false safety warnings. The adapter now uses the provider's documented caption bridge and accounts for its flat fee.
revisit_trigger: Ideogram accepts the application compiler's prompt forms directly without degraded quality or false safety failures, or provider pricing changes.

decision: Use Fal-hosted Ideogram 4 as the sole named second image-adapter candidate; map composition-only references to strong transformation with explicit source-content replacement, and keep provider-independent approval locked until the corrected adapter passes the frozen v2 corpus.
rationale: The product owner's intended candidate is Ideogram 4. Fal documents that image-to-image strength 1.0 ignores the input while lower values stay closer, so composition transfer must not use a subject-preserving low strength or a contradictory inspiration instruction.
revisit_trigger: The corrected preserve-composition preflight or full paired evaluation remains below threshold.

decision: Use Ideogram 4 Medium caption expansion for Fast drafts and Large caption expansion for balanced and full standard-endpoint work while retaining exact application preflight and provider output safety checks.
rationale: The frozen typography preflight used a benign balanced prompt that passed application moderation but reproduced a post-render provider safety rejection with Medium expansion; its Large retry succeeded. The Fast endpoint rejects Large and accepts Medium, so expansion must follow the actual endpoint contract. Safety checks are not disabled or weakened.
revisit_trigger: A targeted draft, typography, or full frozen evaluation continues to produce contract or false post-render safety failures.

decision: Treat every Canvas action as an optimistic, device-write-ahead, idempotent batch: project it immediately, flush batches in monotonic client order through a stale-head-independent Canvas admission path, and reconcile confirmation by client_event_id.
rationale: Remote database latency and unrelated stream events must not move the visible board backward, force a person to repeat a gesture, reorder rapid edits, or duplicate an edit after a response is lost. Advisory locks can inform collaborators but may never block the durable operation they describe.
revisit_trigger: The per-project Durable Object sequencer and cross-device WebSocket fan-out in D-0055 are deployed; retain the same write-ahead and idempotency contract behind that transport.
